about: The compact readiness bitmask a ring.receipt carries as `ready` (GUARD_RING_DESIGN section 6.6, G15): bit n set means the row is ON at the moment of the receipt. The phone builds it in RingSound.bits(); the server must read it with this same table. The `detail` of a `shown` receipt is the live sound check, format below.

bits.0: notifications: the app's notifications are on
bits.1: ring_channel: the Call-style alerts channel exists, is not blocked, and has a sound
bits.2: full_screen: full-screen alerts are allowed (always on below Android 14, where no grant exists)
bits.3: dnd_bypass: the ring channel's Do Not Disturb bypass, read back from Android
bits.5: background: background activity is not restricted
bits.6: alarm_volume_ok: the alarm volume is at least 30 percent of its maximum
bits.7: alarm_tone: the phone has an alarm tone set
bits.8: screen_lock: the phone has a secure screen lock
bits.9: alarm_volume_on: the alarm volume is above 0

detail.soundOn: imp >= 4 AND snd = 1 AND vol > 0 AND dnd = pass; anything else, dnd=unknown included, is 'sound not confirmed'
